_meta.indication: Treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study ALN-TTR02-004 (APOLLO), also referred to as Study 004
pivotal_trials.design: 18-month, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial at 44 sites in 19 countries; patients randomized 2:1 to patisiran 0.3 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults (18 to 85 years) with hATTR amyloidosis with a documented TTR mutation, baseline NIS score of 5 to 130, and PND score less than 3b.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: change from baseline to Month 18 in modified NIS+7 (mNIS+7) score.
pivotal_trials.result: At Month 18, mNIS+7 improved by LS mean of 6 points with patisiran vs worsening of 28 points with placebo; LS mean difference -34.0 points (95% CI -39.9, -28.1; p<0.001). Norfolk-QoL-DN LS mean difference -21.1 (95% CI -27.2, -15.0; p<0.001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10% and >=3% more than placebo) were upper respiratory tract infections (29% vs 21%) and infusion-related reactions (19% vs 9%). Serious AV heart block occurred in 4 patisiran patients (2.7%), including 3 complete AV block, versus none on placebo.
target_moa: Patisiran is a transthyretin-directed small interfering RNA (siRNA) that binds RISC and directs sequence-specific degradation of TTR mRNA in hepatocytes, reducing both wild-type and mutant TTR protein (average 78% reduction in serum TTR).
modality: Oligonucleotide (small interfering RNA, siRNA) formulated as a lipid complex for delivery to hepatocytes.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an advisory committee because the safety profile was acceptable, the trial design was acceptable, and the efficacy findings were clear.

description.text: Updated clinical pharmacology (pharmacodynamics/pharmacokinetics) based on data in patients with prior liver transplantation; no new indication added

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to the clinical pharmacology section (12.2 Pharmacodynamics and 12.3 Pharmacokinetics) of the prescribing information for Onpattro based on data from an open-label study in patients with prior liver transplantation.

summary.text: Patisiran, a new molecular entity, was granted Orphan Drug (6/2012), Fast Track (10/2013), and Breakthrough Therapy (11/2017) designations. It received traditional approval based on the single adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trial APOLLO, not under accelerated approval.

Onpattro (patisiran) is a new molecular entity with a proposed indication for treating polyneuropathy (PN) among adult patients with hATTR-PN.
The applicant has provided data from a single adequate and well-controlled clinical trial as the primary basis of support of the effectiveness of patisiran for the treatment of hATTR-PN.

requirement.text: Establish a worldwide Pregnancy Surveillance Program to collect and analyze information for a minimum of 10 years on pregnancy complications and birth outcomes in women exposed to Onpattro during pregnancy.

citations.quote: 3425-1 Establish a worldwide Pregnancy Surveillance Program to collect and analyze information for a minimum of 10 years on pregnancy complications and birth outcomes in women exposed to Onpattro (patisiran) during pregnancy. Provide a complete protocol which includes details regarding how you plan to encourage patients and providers to report pregnancy exposures (e.g., telephone contact number and/or website in prescribing information), measures to ensure complete data capture regarding pregnancy outcomes and any adverse effects in offspring, and plans for comprehensive data analysis and yearly reporting.
